cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Command words tell you exactly what the examiner expects — misreading them is the most common reason for losing marks

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: 'Describe' requires a straightforward account of what something is or how it works — give factual detail without analysis or evaluation

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: 'Explain' requires you to give reasons or show how something works — go beyond description by showing causes, effects or the reasoning behind a legal principle

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: 'Analyse' requires you to break down a topic into its component parts and examine the relationship between them — identify strengths and weaknesses

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: 'Evaluate' or 'How far' or 'To what extent' requires a balanced assessment with a supported judgement — present arguments for and against and reach a reasoned conclusion

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: 'Compare' requires you to identify similarities and differences between two or more things — use comparative language such as 'whereas', 'similarly', 'in contrast'

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Short-answer questions (1-4 marks) require concise, focused responses — one mark per point, no elaboration needed

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Medium-answer questions (5-10 marks) require developed responses — make a point, explain it and support with an example

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Extended-response questions (15 marks) require a structured essay with an introduction, balanced arguments and a justified conclusion

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: For 15-mark evaluation questions, spend roughly 5 minutes planning and 20 minutes writing — aim for three paragraphs of analysis plus an introduction and conclusion

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Source-based questions require you to use information from the provided source alongside your own legal knowledge — always refer to the source explicitly

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Scenario questions require you to apply legal rules to the facts given — identify the legal issue, state the relevant law, apply it to the facts and reach a conclusion

cards.front: What should you know about gcse law exam tips — command words & question types?
cards.back: 1. For Command Words & Question Types questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Command Words & Question Types 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
